summary: Bill Kenwright, Everton chairman since 2004 and one of the UK's most successful theatre and film producers, has died aged 78, weeks after surgery to remove a cancerous liver tumour. The note recounts his 19 seasons leading Everton, his six-decade career producing over 500 shows, and his early acting role in Coronation Street. It also includes tributes from his family, club owner Farhad Moshiri, Wayne Rooney, Jamie Carragher, Andy Burnham and Sir Ian McKellen.
one_line: Everton chairman and prolific West End theatre producer Bill Kenwright died aged 78 after liver cancer surgery complications, prompting widespread tributes.
key_facts: Bill Kenwright died aged 78; his family said he 'passed away peacefully' on Monday night, with the death announced on Tuesday.

Kenwright had surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his liver about eight weeks before his death; Everton said the operation was 'completely successful' but complications required a 'prolonged period in an intensive care unit'.
Kenwright had been on the Everton board since 1989 and became chairman at Goodison Park in 2004, making him the club's longest-serving chairman for more than a century.
He spent 19 seasons as chairman, overseeing 12 finishes inside the Premier League top eight, including fourth place in 2005, and an FA Cup final appearance in 2009.
In February 2016 Kenwright sold a 49.9% stake in Everton to Iranian businessman Farhad Moshiri, who increased his shares to 94% in January 2022.
In September 2023 Moshiri agreed to sell his 94% stake to American investment fund 777 Partners; Kenwright worked on the takeover until the day of his operation.

Last season an Everton fans' group called for Kenwright to be sacked, saying it had 'no confidence' in him; the board could not attend home games from January after 'threatening correspondence' before a game against Southampton.
Kenwright played Gordon Clegg in Coronation Street between 1968 and 2012, debuting in 1968 as the son of Rovers Return barmaid Betty.
He was awarded a CBE for services to film and theatre in the 2001 New Years Honours List.
His career spanned six decades and included more than 500 West End, Broadway, UK touring and international productions, films and music albums.

He found major success with Blood Brothers and Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat, and also staged The Shawshank Redemption, The Exorcist, Cabaret, Evita, Saturday Night Fever and The Sound of Music.
Sir Ian McKellen is currently starring in Kenwright's production Frank and Percy in London, while Twelve Angry Men, Calendar Girls The Musical, Heathers The Musical and Blood Brothers are on tour.
Wayne Rooney called Kenwright a 'big inspiration' who had a huge impact on his career; Jamie Carragher praised Everton's support around the Hillsborough memorial.
